newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: RIGHTISTS BLAST SWISS SQUAD FOR NOT SINGING ANTHEM.
newsitem.headline: RIGHTISTS BLAST SWISS SQUAD FOR NOT SINGING ANTHEM.

text.p: Swiss nationalists denounced the country's soccer squad on Thursday for not singing along when the Swiss anthem is played at the start of international matches.
"Singing the national anthem is a display of pride in one's own country," the Swiss Democrats, the second-biggest far-right opposition party in parliament, said in a statment.
It complained players had failed to sing when the "Psalm of Switzerland" was played at the start of a World Cup qualification match on Sunday against Finland that ended 3-2 for the Swiss.
"The players did not sing at all and some were even chewing gum," said Bernhard Hess, secretary-general of the party best know for demanding tougher laws against immigrants and other foreigners.
Swiss crowds rarely join when the music is played because the anthem is widely seen as difficult to sing and effusively religious:
"You arrive in the red sky of morning,
I see you bathed in a sea of rays,
Under Switzerland's multi-lingual system, the anthem can be sung in any of the three major tongues -- German, French or Italian.

The government decided only in 1961 that an official anthem was needed at all, replacing a popular but bloodthirsty battle song -- "Do You Call, O Fatherland?" -- that harked back to Switzerland's martial medeival beginnings.

The Swiss Football Federation said players' singing was not an issue until recently, when the side started getting more attention at home by reaching this year's European Cup for the first time since the 1960s.
"We certainly don't want to force anybody to sing. We're thinking about hiring a singer or something like that to motivate the players to join in," a spokesman said.
